(i) **Allenes:** These are hydrocarbons containing two adjacent cumulative double bonds (cumulated dienes) with the general formula $R_2C=C=CR_2$. Substituted allenes lacking a plane of symmetry exhibit axial chirality and show optical isomerism even in the absence of a traditional chiral carbon.

(ii) **Spiranes (Spiro compounds):** These are bicyclic organic compounds featuring rings connected by a single common atom (the spiro atom). Depending on the substituents on the rings, spiro compounds can also display axial chirality and optical isomerism.
proTip: Highlight that neither allenes nor spiranes require a traditional asymmetric carbon to show optical activity; their stereoisomerism arises due to axial chirality.
